assessment: This is a short but incisive report on the biophysical basis of the "size principle" – an old hypothesis to explain the orderly recruitment of interneurons and motorneurons according to the size of their motor pool. The authors examine the contribution of electrical gap junctions to these recruitment phenomena in the spinal locomotor circuits in larval zebrafish. They show that the prevalence of mixed electrical/chemical synapses helps resolve some paradoxical deviations from the size principle. This is an important idea and is based on a convincing analysis of a large electrophysiology dataset acquired over many years.
